# telnyx_tailscale_subnet_router (Resource)

A Tailscale subnet router on a network that advertises the network's routes to your tailnet. Create enrolls it with a Tailscale auth key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "tailscale_auth_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# The auth key is write-only: it is sent on create and never stored. Bump
# auth_key_wo_version to send a replacement after a failed enrollment.
resource "telnyx_tailscale_subnet_router" "office" {
  name              = "office"
  network_id        = telnyx_network.office.id
  region_code       = "ashburn-va"
  advertised_routes = ["10.10.0.0/24"]
  auth_key_wo       = var.tailscale_auth_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `advertised_routes` (Set of String) IPv4 subnets of the Network that the router advertises to the tailnet. Each entry is a canonical CIDR that the Network routes. Default, loopback, link-local, multicast, and Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`) ranges are rejected. So are ranges that overlap the router's own, `172.27.254.0/24` and `198.18.0.0/20`.
- `auth_key_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) A Tailscale auth key that enrolls the router in the user's tailnet: reusable, pre-approved, tagged, and not ephemeral. Telnyx stores it encrypted until enrollment succeeds, then discards it. It is never returned. Write-only: never stored in state. Change `auth_key_wo_version` to send a new value.
- `name` (String) A user specified name for the router.
- `network_id` (String) The id of the Network the router is attached to.
- `region_code` (String) The code of the region the router is created in. `GET /network_coverage` lists the regions whose `available_services` include `tailscale_subnet_router`.

### Optional

- `auth_key_wo_version` (Number) Change this number to send `auth_key_wo` again; Terraform cannot detect a change to a value it does not store.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was created.
- `customer_address` (String) The router's address on the Network, from `172.27.254.0/24`. Tailnet traffic enters the Network from this address.
- `device_id` (String) The router's node id on the tailnet. Set once the router has enrolled.
- `id` (String) Identifies the resource.
- `record_type` (String) Identifies the type of the resource.
- `status` (String) `provisioning`: Telnyx is creating the router or applying a change. `provisioned`: the router is on the tailnet and advertises its routes; the tailnet still approves them. `failed`: enrollment did not complete, and `PATCH` retries it. `deleting`: the router is being removed.
- `tailnet_name` (String) The name of the tailnet the router is enrolled in. Set once the router has enrolled.
- `tailscale_ips` (List of String) The router's addresses on the tailnet. Empty until the router has enrolled.
- `updated_at` (String) ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when the resource was updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import telnyx_tailscale_subnet_router.example <id>
```
